title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go and version bumps

description:
Context and motivation:
This PR unifies several ergonomics and parity gaps across Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) focused on authentication handling, retry behavior, streaming APIs, and a coordinated version bump to 1.27.0. The goal is to make default behaviours consistent across languages so product teams have predictable semantics when switching client libraries or running multi-service integrations.

Summary of changes (single continuous description):
- Auth: introduce a common AuthProvider abstraction (library-level) and token refresh callbacks. SDKs now accept either raw API keys or an AuthProvider implementation; token refresh is performed transparently and synchronized to avoid thundering herds. We consolidated header names and removed inconsistencies where some SDKs sent Authorization vs X-Api-Key. Backwards compatible: passing a string API key follows previous behaviour.
- Retries: standardise default RetryPolicy across sdks: transient (5xx, network errors, 429) with exponential backoff + full jitter, capped retries (max_attempts=6), and safe idempotency checks for streaming endpoints. We added a RetryConfig object/class in each SDK to allow advanced customization and a small integration helper for server-side idempotency tokens.
- Streaming ergonomics: provide a higher-level StreamClient that exposes async iterators (Python/TS) and a channel-like API for Go. Key improvements: built-in backpressure handling (client signals max outstanding chunks), easy cancelation (context propagation in Go), consistent chunk shape (meta, data, done), and explicit reconnect hooks for resumable streams. Streaming handlers now expose a typed event envelope to simplify parse/dispatch.
- Parity fixes and parameter alignment: normalized commonly used parameter names across sdks (model -> model_name, timeout -> request_timeout, max_tokens -> max_output_tokens). Updated TypeScript typings to match Python/Go shapes and tightened Go structs for better compile-time checks.
- Tests, docs, and CI: added cross-language integration tests for auth+streaming, fixed flaky test discovered in streaming backpressure scenario, updated SDK docs and migration notes, and extended CI matrix to run smoke streaming tests.
- Version bumps: coordinated SDK version bump to 1.27.0 for Python/TS/Go and updated changelogs and publish scripts.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Default retry policy changed (more conservative). Customers relying on very-low retry counts should pin RetryConfig or pass max_attempts.
- AuthProvider is additive: existing API key usage is unchanged. Advanced users can implement AuthProvider to supply tokens from KMS/HSM or short-lived tokens.
- Streaming API changes are mostly additive/ergonomic; breakages are unlikely but users who implemented low-level stream parsing may need to adapt to the typed envelope.

Related work and references:
- Related Linear: ENG-4123 (sdk auth parity), ENG-4199 (streaming ergonomics rollup).
- Previous PRs addressing auth/retries/streaming: pr-18432, pr-21789 (historical).

Testing and CI notes:
- Initial integration run failed due to streaming timing flakiness; added small delay in test harness and added a backpressure stress test. After fixes all CI checks passed.

Merge outcome:
- Squash merge into main, tags created for 1.27.0 on each SDK package and packages published to internal artifact registry.

release_notes:
- SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) bumped to v1.27.0.
- Unified AuthProvider with transparent token refresh and consistent header semantics.
- Standardized retry policy across SDKs: exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency helpers for streaming.
- StreamClient API improved: backpressure, cancelation, typed event envelopes, and resume hooks.
- Parameter name parity: model_name / request_timeout / max_output_tokens.
- Updated docs and cross-language integration tests.
